notes.28136.4.7: Lines 4.7-4.8 belong to another tablet (28136) and keep only the letters SI and RE at the ends of lost lines; they cannot be translated. In 52736 the spelling is non-standard throughout (marked (!) by the edition). 'accedat morbo cotidea' has no expressed subject: if morbo stands for morbus, 'may disease come upon [her] daily'; taken as written, 'may [she] come to disease daily'. In cos[i]lio(m) ('mind', literally 'counsel') one letter is restored.

nodes.text: Gods of the underworld, I ask you to take up the name
Luxsia, daughter of Aulus Antestius: head, heart, mind, health,
life, all her limbs; may disease come upon [her] daily, and
if you do [this], I will pay the vow that I am making, as you deserve.
